question.:question/problem:
Differentiate $f(t)+g(t)$ with respect to $t$, given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨3 t - 1,\,3 t - 18,\,- 14 t⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨t^{2},\,3 t^{2} - 3,\,- 2 t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By the sum rule, we have

$$
(f(t)+g(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t - 1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t - 18),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 14 t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,3,\,-14⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t^{2} - 3),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 2 t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2 t,\,6 t,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨3,\,3,\,-14⟩+⟨2 t,\,6 t,\,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨2 t + 3,\,6 t + 3,\,-16⟩\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:

$$
(f(t)+g(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t)
$$

$$

question.:question/problem:
Differentiate $f(t)+4g(t)$ with respect to $t$, given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨- 2 \sqrt{t},\,\log{\left(t \right)},\,-4⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨- 2 t,\,\frac{1}{t},\,- 2 t^{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the constant multiple rule and the sum rule, we have

$$
(f(t)+4g(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+4{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 2 \sqrt{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\log{\left(t \right)}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4)⟩ \\  & =⟨- \frac{1}{\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{1}{t},\,0⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 2 t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 2 t^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,- \frac{1}{t^{2}},\,- 8 t^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+4g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+4{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨- \frac{1}{\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{1}{t},\,0⟩+4⟨-2,\,- \frac{1}{t^{2}},\,- 8 t^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨- \frac{1}{\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{1}{t},\,0⟩+⟨-8,\,- \frac{4}{t^{2}},\,- 32 t^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨-8 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{t - 4}{t^{2}},\,- 32 t^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨-8 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{t - 4}{t^{2}},\,- 32 t^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:

$$

question.:question/problem:
Differentiate $f(t)+g(t)+h(t)$ with respect to $t$, where

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨4,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨4 t,\,0,\,t⟩ \\ h(t) & =⟨4 t^{2},\,0,\,t^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the sum rule, we can write

$$
(f(t)+g(t)+h(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t)+{h}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4 t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {h}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4 t^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨8 t,\,0,\,2 t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+g(t)+h(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t)+{h}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,0⟩+⟨4,\,0,\,1⟩+⟨8 t,\,0,\,2 t⟩ \\  & =⟨8 t + 4,\,0,\,2 t + 1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the value of $(2f(t)-g(t))^{′}$ at $t=-1,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨- 16 \sqrt{3 - t},\,\sin{\left(\pi t \right)},\,3 \log{\left(- 2 t \right)}⟩, \\ g(t) & =⟨2 t \left(1 - t\right),\,\pi t^{2},\,3 - 3 t^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, notice that

$$
(2f(t)-g(t))^{′}=2{f}^{′}(t)-{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 16 \sqrt{3 - t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sin{\left(\pi t \right)}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 \log{\left(- 2 t \right)})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{8}{\sqrt{3 - t}},\,\pi \cos{\left(\pi t \right)},\,\frac{3}{t}⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2 t \left(1 - t\right)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\pi t^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 - 3 t^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2 - 4 t,\,2 \pi t,\,- 6 t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(2f(t)-g(t))^{′}\big|_{t=-1} & =2{f}^{′}(-1)-{g}^{′}(-1) \\  & =2⟨4,\,- \pi,\,-3⟩-⟨6,\,- 2 \pi,\,6⟩ \\  & =2⟨4,\,- \pi,\,-3⟩-⟨6,\,- 2 \pi,\,6⟩ \\  & =⟨8,\,- 2 \pi,\,-6⟩-⟨6,\,- 2 \pi,\,6⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,-12⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the derivative of $-2f(t)+2g(t)$ with respect to $t$, where

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t)&=(4 t^{2} + 1)\,i- \frac{4}{t - 3}\,j+\cos{\left(3 t \right)}\,k \\ g(t)&=(t - 4)\,i+e^{4 t}\,j+\cos{\left(3 t \right)}\,k\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the constant multiple rule and the sum rule, we have

$$
(-2f(t)+2g(t))'=-2f'(\!t)+2g'(\!t).
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(t)&=⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4 t^{2} + 1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- \frac{4}{t - 3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\cos{\left(3 t \right)})⟩ \\ &=8 t\,i+\frac{4}{\left(t - 3\right)^{2}}\,j- 3 \sin{\left(3 t \right)}\,k \\ g'(t)&=⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t - 4),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(e^{4 t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\cos{\left(3 t \right)})⟩ \\ &=1\,i+4 e^{4 t}\,j- 3 \sin{\left(3 t \right)}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2f(t)+2g(t))'&=-2f'(\!t)+2g'(\!t) \\ &=-2\left(8 t\,i+\frac{4}{\left(t - 3\right)^{2}}\,j- 3 \sin{\left(3 t \right)}\,k\right)+2\left(1\,i+4 e^{4 t}\,j- 3 \sin{\left(3 t \right)}\,k\right) \\ &=\left(- 16 t\,i- \frac{8}{\left(t - 3\right)^{2}}\,j+6 \sin{\left(3 t \right)}\,k\right)+\left(2\,i+8 e^{4 t}\,j- 6 \sin{\left(3 t \right)}\,k\right) \\ &=(2 - 16 t)\,i+(8 e^{4 t} - \frac{8}{\left(t - 3\right)^{2}})\,j.\end{aligned}
$$
